# The worksheet as a document
Text cells are Markdown with tables, quotes, footnotes and images. Values from the worksheet appear in sentences with `{{expr}}` and stay live. Another saved worksheet can be imported. The title block above opens **Document**: author, export to HTML or Markdown, print to PDF, and the version history.

## A sentence with live numbers
The RC circuit imported above has a time constant of {{tau -> ms}}, so after one second the capacitor sits at {{v_c(1 s) -> V}}, which is {{v_c(1 s)/V_s * 100}} percent of the supply[^1]. Change $R$ below and the sentence follows.

[^1]: The charging curve is $v_c(t) = V_s (1 - e^{-t/\tau})$.

R = 2.2 kohm
tau = R C -> s

## Tables, quotes and display math
| quantity | symbol | value |
|---|:---:|---:|
| resistance | $R$ | {{R}} |
| capacitance | $C$ | {{C -> uF}} |
| time constant | $\tau$ | {{tau -> ms}} |

> Five time constants and the capacitor is charged for all practical purposes: {{(1 - exp(-5)) * 100}} percent.

$$ i(t) = C \frac{dv_c}{dt} = \frac{V_s}{R} e^{-t/\tau} $$

## Images and links
Upload a picture with **Data** and write `![caption](name.png)`; links work as `[text](https://example.org)`. Numbered steps:
1. save this worksheet under a name
2. change something and save again
3. open **Document** to compare the two versions or restore the older one

---
Export HTML gives one file with the math rendered; Export Markdown keeps the LaTeX.
